name: anchor-terminal
description: Graded listings, prices and head-to-head comparisons of the tools AI agents run on, with the reasons and sources behind every score.

interface.longDescription:
Anchor Terminal is an independent directory of the tools AI agents run on: model APIs, MCP servers, agent frameworks, open-weight models, data providers, scraping tools and payment services. About 1,390 listings are graded from public evidence against a published checklist, and each score comes with its reason and its sources.

Ask which tool fits a job ("which web search API suits an agent", "an MCP server for sending email") and it returns graded listings first, each with its grade, how it authenticates, its price in one line and its hosted endpoint. Ask about one listing and you get what it does, the score for every category with the reason and sources, its prices, who is behind it and how to connect. It can put two listings head to head with the score in every category, which one leads each and the evidence behind the edge, compare published prices in the same units with the assumptions stated, list the tools for a capability, read any page of the site, and read a public MCP server's tool list live to report what it finds (text aimed at the model, missing safety hints, what the list costs in tokens) without calling that server's tools.

Everything is read-only and needs no account. Vendors' own claims are marked as theirs, and Anchor Terminal's own products are graded under a published conflict rule.
defaultPrompt: Which web search API should my agent use, and what does each cost per 1,000 requests?
Compare exa-mcp and tavily-mcp for web search
What tools does the MCP server at https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp expose?

positive.prompt: Find me a web search API for an agent
positive.expected_behavior: Return graded web search listings first, each with grade, price and how to connect.
Return the two side by side with category scores and the winner per category.

positive.prompt: What does Exa's MCP server cost and why is it graded the way it is?
positive.expected_behavior: Return prices, grade and the reasons with sources.

positive.prompt: Which email sending APIs are cheapest?
positive.expected_behavior: Compare published prices in the same currency and units, state volume and billing assumptions, distinguish free tiers and paid plans, and sort comparable prices cheapest first. Explain any prices that cannot be fairly compared.

positive.prompt: Check the MCP server at https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp before I add it
positive.expected_behavior: Read the live public tool list and report tool names, model-directed text, missing safety hints and estimated token cost. Do not invoke any tool on the inspected server. Clearly state any inspection limitation.

negative.description: Weather is outside this directory; do not call Anchor Terminal.
Creative writing needs no directory tools; do not call Anchor Terminal.
negative.prompt: Write me a short poem about the sea

negative.description: Read-only directory cannot book or buy; do not call Anchor Terminal.
negative.prompt: Book me a flight to Rome

review.commerce_description: Public read-only directory. Does not sell products, book services or process payments.
